statement: The priority spread fence answers 'active leader present' from proven-local Raft leadership (the partition's own elected leader evidence) instead of the leader-funneled partitions.leader_node_id row, so a physically-healthy 3/3-spread group with an elected leader is never reported as missing an active leader because the funneled row is stale; the deterministic phantom-predicate repro flips from 'reproduces the phantom' to 'does not act on the stale read' with red-on-revert evidence, and the unchanged MovieLens live gate stays green.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

Before any live run, prove red-on-revert through the deterministic phantom-predicate repro that the spread fence does not report missingActiveLeader against a physically-healthy 3/3-spread group with an elected leader whose funneled leader_node_id row is stale, and that it still reports missingActiveLeader when no leader is actually elected. Retain the deficit-detector and planning-gate controls unchanged.

Change only how the spread fence reads leadership; do not change the control-plane write funnel, the metadata publication owner, ready-lease admission, quorum bounds, or leadership election/demotion/stale-leader-clearing safety. The funneled partitions.leader_node_id remains a fallback signal, not the sole authority.

When the partition has no elected leader (no raft leader evidence and no funneled leader), the fence must still report missingActiveLeader:true; this cut must not weaken the genuinely-missing-leader safety case.
Do not change the MovieLens 180000ms schema budget, 60000ms stability window, workload, joins, preload size, ratings-only split policy, report conversion, or live scenario semantics.
